title: Situational judgement tests
examples: How do I decide which action is best when several options seem okay?
What is the difference between choosing the best action and ranking them?
Can you give me an example of ranking responses in a workplace setting?

explain.say: Today we are learning to rank responses in judgment tests. This means putting actions in order of best to worst. You must decide the best course of action first.

items: Step 3: Rank these actions from best to worst.

explain.say: First, you must fully analyze the situation presented to you. Look for all the key pieces of information given. This helps you understand the core problem needing a solution.
Next, you should consider all the possible actions you could take. Do not eliminate any idea too early. Think broadly about what could reasonably help resolve the issue.
Then, you must rank these actions from best to worst. The top choice is the most effective and appropriate response. The bottom choice is least helpful or potentially harmful.
For example, if a client is upset about a delay, the best action is to first apologize sincerely. Then, you should provide a clear revised timeline for completion.
In a real work scenario, imagine a team meeting is running over time. The best action is to suggest a time limit for each agenda item. This keeps the meeting productive and focused.

items: Suggest time limits for each topic

faq.q: Does ranking mean I have to choose only one action?
faq.a: No, ranking means putting them in order of preference. You are showing the sequence of best to worst.
asks: Do I pick just the top one?
Is it a list or a single choice?

faq.q: Should I consider my own feelings when ranking responses?
faq.a: You should focus only on what is professionally appropriate and effective. Personal feelings should not guide your ranking.
asks: Should I prioritize what feels easiest?

faq.q: What if two actions seem equally good?
faq.a: If two actions are equally good, you might rank them as tied or look for a secondary benefit. Look for the one that solves more problems.
asks: Can I put two things on the same rank?
How do I break a tie?

faq.q: Is there a general rule for ranking responses?
faq.a: There is no single rule, but always prioritize safety, then immediate impact, then long-term solutions.
asks: Is there a hierarchy I must follow?
What is the most important rule?

faq.q: How much time should I spend on analyzing the situation?
faq.a: Spend enough time to be sure you have all the facts. Do not rush this initial analysis phase under any circumstances.
asks: Should I spend most of my time reading?
Is analysis more important than choosing?

facts: Ranking requires ordering options from most effective to least effective.
Analysis involves gathering all known facts about the scenario.
The best action addresses the root cause, not just the symptoms.
Professional judgment requires balancing immediate needs with long-term goals.

quiz.say: A colleague misses a deadline, causing a project delay. Which is the best first step?
quiz.show: Colleague Missed Deadline: Best First Step?

options.show: D. Start working on the delayed part yourself.
options.say: D. Start working on the delayed part yourself.

options.show: A. Privately ask for an update and support.
options.say: A. Privately ask for an update and support.

options.show: B. Immediately tell the manager about the delay.
options.say: B. Immediately tell the manager about the delay.

options.show: C. Send a group email reminding everyone of the deadline.
options.say: C. Send a group email reminding everyone of the deadline.

quiz.why: This respects the colleague's dignity and gathers necessary information before escalating.

wrong.0: This avoids accountability and might lead to duplicated or incorrect work.
wrong.2: This is too confrontational and might damage trust before understanding the issue.
wrong.3: This is accusatory and does not address the specific colleague's need for help.

quiz.say: You notice a minor policy breach by a peer. What is the most appropriate initial response?

options.show: D. Publicly correct the peer in front of others.
options.say: D. Publicly correct the peer in front of others.

options.show: A. Speak to the peer privately and gently.
options.say: A. Speak to the peer privately and gently.

options.show: B. Report it immediately to Human Resources.
options.say: B. Report it immediately to Human Resources.

options.show: C. Ignore it, hoping the peer corrects themselves.
options.say: C. Ignore it, hoping the peer corrects themselves.

quiz.why: A private conversation allows for correction without causing public embarrassment.

wrong.0: Public correction damages relationships and makes the peer defensive.
wrong.2: This is an overreaction and skips the chance for peer-to-peer correction.
wrong.3: Ignoring a breach means the problem might continue or worsen over time.

quiz.say: A key piece of equipment breaks down unexpectedly. What is the best immediate action?

options.show: B. Follow the established emergency protocol.
options.say: B. Follow the established emergency protocol.

options.show: A. Try to fix it using personal knowledge.
options.say: A. Try to fix it using personal knowledge.

options.show: C. Wait until the end of the day to report it.
options.say: C. Wait until the end of the day to report it.

options.show: D. Ask a colleague who seems knowledgeable to fix it.
options.say: D. Ask a colleague who seems knowledgeable to fix it.

quiz.why: Protocols are designed by experts to ensure safety and efficiency in crises.

wrong.1: This risks injury or causing further, unmanageable damage.
wrong.2: Delaying the report prevents necessary maintenance and replacement scheduling.
wrong.3: Relying on guesswork from others is unreliable and unsafe.
